heading: INT. LUNAR LAVA TUBE - GREENHOUSE - ARTIFICIAL DAY

units.text: INT. LUNAR LAVA TUBE - GREENHOUSE - ARTIFICIAL DAY
A cathedral of black basalt, strung with grow-lamps.
Rows of tomatoes and soybeans climb trellises under a violet glow.
Condensation drips from a vaulted ceiling.
DR. PALOMA REYNOSO, 40s, in a canvas apron over a thermal suit, prunes a tomato vine with delicate care.
Behind her, an airlock hisses.
A figure in a worn pressure suit steps through, visor fogged.
It stops three paces inside and stands very still, as if afraid to wake the plants.
You're not on the roster.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: No. I came on the supply drone.
units.name: THE VISITOR

units.text: The drone carries cargo.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: I was cargo.
units.name: THE VISITOR

units.text: Paloma sets down her shears.
She approaches, slowly, until she can see through the visor to the face behind it: gaunt, unshaven, eyes red.
Take off your helmet.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: I'd rather not.
units.name: THE VISITOR

units.text: Then you can't stay.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: He lifts his hands to the seals.
The helmet rotates with a hiss.
He draws a breath of the humid air and closes his eyes.
The scent of tomatoes fills the cave.
Who are you?
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: Orin Feld. Systems tech, Tycho Base. I left four years ago.
units.name: THE VISITOR

units.text: Paloma staggers back against a trellis.
The tomatoes sway.
Orin Feld died on the surface. We held a service.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: I know. I was there. In the back.
units.name: ORIN

units.text: You were dead.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: For a while. It was easier.
units.name: ORIN

units.text: Paloma slaps him.
The crack echoes off the basalt.
Orin does not lift a hand.
He just stands, helmet under one arm, cheek reddening.
Four years. Four years, Orin.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: Paloma--
units.name: ORIN

units.text: Dr. Reynoso, to you.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: She turns away, shoulders shaking, and presses her palm to a vine.
A tomato drops into her hand.
She stares at it.
It's the first one, isn't it?
units.name: ORIN

units.text: The first red one. Yes.
units.name: PALOMA

units.text: Eat it.
units.name: ORIN

units.text: She does not move.
He steps forward, takes it gently from her fingers, and bites into it.
Juice runs down his chin.
He laughs.
He is crying.
God. I forgot.
units.name: ORIN

units.text: Paloma looks at him.
Slowly, she smiles, and reaches for another.
